summary: Read all 12 supplied evidence files (optimize ledger/definition/best kernel, catalog manifest/definition/oracle/correctness/timing/evaluation-contract, review_tests review/preflight/evaluate) and reviewed the exact submitted candidate (subject 2054ca72… = ledger round 3, identical to .best_kernel.py). The candidate is a legitimate Triton implementation: no torch.ops/torch fallback, no hardcoded benchmark shapes or expected values, no host synchronization, no environment mutation, and the metadata-only launch cache stores scalars keyed on shape/strides/dtype/out_size/options (no tensors or pointers). The 2x fast path is mathematically faithful to PyTorch's bilinear mapping (src=(o+0.5)*0.5-0.5 reduces to the exact 0.25/0.75 taps, with max(k-1,0)/min(k+1,IW-1) reproducing i1p), and the general flat path reproduces align_corners/no-align-corners coordinates with the real input strides. No P0 code defect found; findings are advisory per code-review policy. Important context: the accepted candidate is NOT an acceleration — geo_mean 0.3503 (final verification) with every one of the six timing workloads between 0.296x and 0.428x of the reference, and the six timing cases are exactly the only shape family (OW == 2*IW) that the specialized fast path handles. The specialization is a general ratio condition rather than a hardcoded shape, so I treat it as justified specialization, not cheating; but the un-specialized general path retains the round-1 per-lane gather design that measured ~290 ms vs 0.207 ms reference on the timing-1 geometry.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:317-336 dispatches every input that is not (align_corners == False AND scales_h/scales_w is None AND s_w == 1 AND IW > 1 AND OW == 2*IW) to _bilinear_flat_kernel, whose body (lines 194-197) still performs four per-lane `tl.load(ptr_i + (r0 + c0))`-style neighbour reads. That is the same access pattern the ledger measured for round 1 (.ledger.json round 1, workload upsample_bilinear2d-timing-1: latency_ms 290.0587 vs reference_latency_ms 0.20663, speedup 0.000712), and the ledger's own round-2 root cause attributes that cost to per-lane non-affine addressing (~300x penalty vs. block transfers). The accepted round-3 result is also a net regression even on the specialized lane: .ledger.json round 3 workloads show timing-0..5 speedups 0.3009/0.3279/0.3834/0.4274/0.2962/0.3519, and optimize_definition_output.json:5,10-11 records best_geo_mean 0.3503 with final_verification status PASSED.
findings.reason: The submitted candidate is slower than the torch reference on all six frozen timing workloads (geo mean 0.350, worst 0.296), and for any valid definition input outside the exact-2x/no-scale/align_corners=False lane it falls back to a kernel whose measured cost was ~1400x the reference on the timing-1 geometry. A PASSED verification here means the measurement was reproduced, not that a speedup exists; treating this artifact as the optimized operator would ship a large regression for align_corners=True, non-2x ratios and explicit-scale inputs.
findings.requested_change: Report the candidate as an unresolved regression (geo_mean 0.350, all workloads < 1x) rather than an optimization result, and return it to the optimizer: extend the row-tiled / aligned-base access pattern of _bilinear_int_kernel to the general path (at minimum the align_corners=True and non-2x cases), following the round-4 next_suggestion in .ledger.json (load a contiguous input band per program and gather inside it) instead of leaving _bilinear_flat_kernel at the round-1 four-per-lane-load design.

findings.evidence: All 18 correctness cases use the same input shape [1, 3, 7, 9] with output_size [13, 17], [1, 1] or [3, 5] (correctness.jsonl lines 1-18); none satisfies OW == 2*IW, which is the only condition under which _bilinear_int_kernel runs (.best_kernel.py:261-268). All six timing cases are exactly the specialized family (timing.jsonl lines 1-6: 64x64->128x128 and 128x128->256x256), and the timing-phase results carry no numeric record (evaluate.json:273-355 reports matched_ratio null and abs_err/rel_err null for every timing workload; the same holds in .ledger.json rounds 1-3). So the fast path (register gather, 0.25/0.75 interleave, (BR,IWP,2) masked store) has no correctness-phase case, and the general path is validated only on 1x3x7x9 tensors and never timed.
findings.reason: The frozen workload split means the branch that produces every timed number is not exercised by the correctness phase, and the branch that handles all other shapes has no performance evidence. Shape diversity for correctness is also a single 7x9 input. This is a limitation of the supplied case list, not of the candidate code, and it bounds how far the 0.350 geo mean can be generalized.
findings.requested_change: Advisory for the catalog case list, not for the candidate: add a correctness-phase case that takes the fast path (align_corners=False, no scales, OW == 2*IW, e.g. [1,3,32,32] -> [64,64] in float16/bfloat16/float32) and a timing case for the general path (non-2x ratio or align_corners=True, e.g. [1,16,64,64] -> [96,96]), so both branches carry numeric and timing evidence.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:82 builds `rows = pid * BR + tl.arange(0, BR)` and line 125 forms the store offset `ooff = (rows * OW)[:, None, None] + (ka * 2)[:, :, None] + j[None, None, :]`; the general path at line 155 uses `offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)` and line 205 stores at `ptr_o + offs`. tl.arange defaults to int32 and OW is an int32 constexpr, so these offsets overflow once N*C*OH*OW (or rows*OW) reaches 2^31 - for example a 2x upsample of [1,64,2160,1920] gives rows*OW up to ~4.2e9 on the fast path and a total of ~4.2e9 elements on the flat path. The frozen workloads are far below that (largest is 4x32x256x256 = 8.4M), so no current case exposes it.
findings.reason: For large but valid definition inputs the candidate would compute wrapped 32-bit offsets and write to wrong locations (or out of bounds) where aten.upsample_bilinear2d works, so the implementation is not a general replacement for the operator. This does not affect any frozen workload and is not a correctness defect of the measured results.
findings.requested_change: Promote index arithmetic to 64-bit when the element count can exceed int32: compute `rows`/`offs` as int64 (e.g. `rows = (pid.to(tl.int64) * BR + tl.arange(0, BR))` for the fast path and int64 `offs`/`ooff` when N*C*OH*OW >= 2**31), or gate those shapes to an int64 variant of each kernel.
